subject: Cloud Computing
title: Real-Time Streaming Data
description: Learn Real-Time Streaming Data in one minute.

hook.text: A ride-sharing app processes millions of GPS updates per second. Batch processing would be too slow. It needs real-time.

buildup.text: Streaming platforms process data as it arrives: Kafka, Kinesis, and Pub/Sub handle millions of events per second.

discovery.text: Streaming enables live dashboards, fraud detection, and instant recommendations — all reacting to data in real time.

twist.text: Streaming is complex. Handling out-of-order events, duplicates, and failures requires careful engineering.

climax.text: The world is moving from batch to real-time. Businesses that react in seconds beat those that react in hours.

punchline.text: Batch is yesterday's data. Streaming is what's happening now.

quiz.question: What makes streaming data processing challenging?
options: Handling out-of-order events, duplicates, and failures in real time
Streaming can only process text data, not numbers
Cloud providers charge 10x more for streaming than batch

details.summary: Real-time streaming processes data continuously as it arrives rather than in batches. Apache Kafka, Amazon Kinesis, and Google Pub/Sub ingest millions of events per second for use cases like fraud detection, live analytics, and IoT telemetry.
details.whyItMatters: Batch processing introduces delays that are unacceptable for fraud detection, monitoring, and real-time personalization. Streaming lets organizations act on data in seconds instead of hours.
takeaways: Events are processed continuously as they arrive
Kafka, Kinesis, and Pub/Sub handle millions of events per second
Enables fraud detection, live dashboards, and IoT processing

faq.question: What is Apache Kafka?
faq.answer: Kafka is a distributed event streaming platform that stores and processes ordered streams of events. It acts as a durable, high-throughput message broker. Kafka is the de facto standard for real-time data pipelines and powers streaming at companies like LinkedIn and Uber.

faq.question: When should you use streaming instead of batch?
faq.answer: Use streaming when data freshness matters in seconds or minutes: fraud detection, monitoring alerts, live recommendations, and real-time analytics. Use batch when daily or hourly freshness is sufficient and processing logic is complex or resource-intensive.
